newsitem.title: CHINA: China is second biggest nonferrous metals producer.
newsitem.headline: China is second biggest nonferrous metals producer.

text.p: China will maintain its position as the world's second largest nonferrous metals producer in 1996, the China Daily said on Tuesday quoting the China National Nonferrous Metals Industry Corporation.
Output of copper, lead, zinc, nickel, aluminium, magnesium, titanium, antimony, tin and mercury is expected to surpass 4.45 million tonnes this year, up by 6.5 percent from 1995, it said.
China plans to turn out 4.55 million tonnes of the 10 nonferrous metals in 1997, with output of copper and aluminium reaching 900,000 tonnes and more than 1.8 million tonnes respectively.
Enterprises directly under the corporation were expected to turn out 2.55 million tonnes of the 10 nonferrous metals this year, it said.
Due to rising costs and price cuts for the main nonferrous metal, the industry suffered a drop in economic returns in the first half of this year, it said.
The whole corporation was estimated to invest 3.0 billion yuan in infrastructure and nearly 1.4 billion yuan in key technology-upgrading projects this year, it said.
The corporation was estimated to handle $1.78 billion in foreign trade, with imports reaching $550 million and exports surpassing $1.1 billion, it said.
The corporation accounts for most of China's output of nonferrous metals.
